quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the wheels, causing you to lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Look around constantly.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look around constantly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots. Always look around for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: A driver should:

options.text: Look straight ahead only.
Focus only on the middle of the road.
Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the sides, ahead, and behind your car.
questions.explanation: Watch all around your car. Good drivers know what is happening everywhere around their vehicle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that traffic may merge from the right, so be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this intersection.

questions.question: If you see a flashing red traffic light, you:

options.text: Are traveling in the wrong direction.
Must treat it like a stop sign.
Cannot go until it turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light the same as a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: What do defensive drivers do?

options.text: They trust that other drivers will do the right thing.
They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect no help and give none.

questions.correctAnswerText: They think about what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means expecting mistakes from other drivers and being ready to handle them.

questions.question: A steady yellow light warns that red is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Continue and clear the intersection safely.
Speed up to avoid an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and clear the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, move through it as quickly and safely as you can.

questions.question: When you see flashing red lights at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the approaching train.
Stop completely.
Drive around any lowered gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn you about trains. Always obey railroad crossing signs and lights. Never try to drive around barriers.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Before you start driving.
Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Also adjust your seat, fasten your seatbelt, and secure loose items. Never adjust mirrors while the car is moving.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at your normal speed.
Brake hard as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast in wet conditions causes hydroplaning. Your tires lose contact with the road and your car slides on water. Slow down when it rains to prevent this.

questions.question: You should signal continuously while turning because it:

options.text: Is required by law.
Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
Is always unsafe to turn it off early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells drivers, riders, and pedestrians what you plan to do.

questions.question: Your wheels have run off the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the steering wheel slightly left to get back on the road.
Hold the steering wheel firm, release the gas, and gently brake.
Brake hard and turn the steering wheel sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firm, release the gas, and gently brake.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently. Let your speed drop, then safely return to the road. Sharp turns can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle on a two-lane road?

options.text: When driving on a hill.
When driving in a curve.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, or in no-passing zones. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for work.
Falling asleep and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes you slower to decide and increases crash risk. You could fall asleep at the wheel and cause a serious or fatal crash.

questions.question: Which is a dangerous habit in work zones?

options.text: Following another vehicle too closely.
Not watching for workers and equipment.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down and do not follow other vehicles closely. Watch carefully for workers and moving equipment.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Stop suddenly.
Turn around and find another route.
Drive through the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded roads. Water can hide hazards. Turn around and take another route.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Does not affect driving.
Does not put others at risk.
Doubles your chance of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chance of a crash.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start going down a steep hill.
Speed up when entering curves and slow down when exiting them.
Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while in a curve can cause you to skid.

questions.question: You must remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must be able to see clearly through all your vehicle's windows. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from your windows and mirrors before you drive.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect light back to you in these conditions, making it harder to see ahead.

questions.question: Driving more slowly than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
Appropriate if you don't know the speed limit.
Often unsafe because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often unsafe because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take dangerous risks to pass you.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No turns.
No outlet.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You may see this sign at intersections where oncoming traffic is common.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with its siren and flashing lights, drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: When driving in heavy fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Speed up so you do not cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam lights. If the fog is very heavy and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait until it clears.

questions.question: If you see heavy smoke ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and continue.
Reduce speed, move right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beam headlights and continue.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce speed, move right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, reduce speed right away, move as far right as possible, and stop off the road. Then decide if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be deadly.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. Increase the distance between you and the car ahead so you have more time to stop if needed. Use headlights correctly at night.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines on the road center mean that passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines in the center mean traffic from either direction cannot cross to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When you are following a small passenger vehicle.
When another driver is tailgating you.
When you are driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another driver is tailgating you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, add extra space ahead of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or change lanes. Do not brake suddenly, as this can cause a crash.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: If you speed up before the turn.
If traffic on that street moves to the right.
If traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic moves to the left and there is no sign forbidding the turn. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: A truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly turn before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes its turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes its turn.
questions.explanation: Never try to squeeze between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus has completely finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean?

options.text: No passing is allowed.
They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed yellow lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden and unsafe lane changes.
They have many passengers in their car.
They drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden and unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers on the road. An aggressive driver often makes sudden or unsafe lane changes. Do not challenge them. The safest thing to do is get out of their way.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead on the road.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead on the road.
questions.explanation: At higher speeds, your vehicle needs more distance to stop. Look far ahead so you have time to react safely to hazards.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas you cannot see when you are tired.
Areas near your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas near your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move. Check the rear corners of your vehicle. These hidden areas are called blind spots because mirrors cannot show them.

questions.question: On a multilane one-way street, which lane should you use to turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The lane closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: You see oncoming traffic on your left and parked cars on your right. Which way should you steer?

options.text: Toward the oncoming traffic side.
Toward the parked cars side.
Down the middle between both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Down the middle between both sides.
questions.explanation: If oncoming traffic is on your left and parked cars are on your right, steer down the middle. This gives you the most space away from both hazards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Reduction in lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Do not turn around on or near curves or hills. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and receive a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your insurance proof and license to an officer after any traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
To keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic and signals from other drivers. Be ready for vehicles entering at on-ramps and sudden changes in road conditions.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right edge and slow down.
Move to the right edge and stop.
Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right edge and stop.
questions.explanation: Let emergency vehicles with flashing lights go first. Move to the right edge and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is crossing the street.
At all times.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Low beam headlights.
Four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are entering a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around.

questions.question: Which of these commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit and driving too fast for conditions cause many crashes. Always drive at legal speeds and adjust for weather and traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your wheels to the right. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When is pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours.
When rain first begins.
After it has been raining for one to two hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first begins.
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first starts. Dirt and oil mix with water, creating a slick coating on the road.
